# E058 / GOV-03 — APERAK caller contract

Base: main71dc255e after #318/#320/#321. PR310 stays paused; no migrations,
generated types, original specifications, grants or replay code are changed.

## Reproduced defects and scope

The source-bound selector introduced by #320 was not receiving its new context
through versionRegistry and kernel/config adapters. Thus selector-only cases
passed while real wrappers threw missing-source errors. The validator also let
source metadata plus persisted version override a contradictory actual UNH.
Naive string splits could reinterpret released delimiters in that UNH.

A shared pure APERAK profile resolver now uses #321's release-aware tokenizer
and UNH parser, requiring the existing exact P tuple96A/E2SE6A or U tuple04A/
E5SE5A. Supplied source-family metadata must agree with the wire. It does not
infer a guide revision from E5SE5A, and is not an authorization/correlation proof.
Effective guide selection stays in the existing guideRegistry/versionSelector.

All canonical versionRegistry methods and public config/kernel wrappers retain
sourceMessageFamily/rawPayload. The two ACK persistence entry points forward
the exact built payload. File registration uses an extracted real adapter with
the same report semantics. Mailbox ingestion records source-profile failures
as a negative version finding while preserving raw data/status for protected
review; it never creates a positive ACK/business outcome from that annotation.
Unrelated errors are not swallowed. A successful recheck clears only its current
profile diagnostic and preserves other evidence and the original input.

The read-only catalogue is deliberately separate from the operational resolver:
unknown source means no selected/current/accepted profile, not a generic P
default or both families marked accepted. Platform rules and three existing
admin consumers use that contract. Auth, tenant filtering and parallel reads
are unchanged. File/mail helpers are moved to small modules so tests execute
the actual adapter code rather than mocks of that logic.

## Verification

The initial39-case actual-source harness produced7passes/32failures on the
pre-fix caller implementation. All corrected cases pass; added adversarial,
file/mail and read-only cases bring the current harness to68/68. Existing
source identity43, PRODAT locators28 and component escaping41 pass:112/112.
All cases load real modules; a DB proxy throws on access and no network is used.

Positive/negative P/U/ERR ACK construction is checked through real envelope
preflight/validator. The matrix covers all four versionRegistry APIs, both sides
of the October boundary, contradictory metadata, wrong directory/association,
released or punctuated tokens, multiple/missing UNH, custom UNA, unknown
operational profile, unrelated failures and unchanged non-APERAK selection.
The receipt-date and input/report preservation checks use the real adapters.

The immutable specification check and unchanged source-size budget pass locally.
The current checkout lacks installed project packages, so full TypeScript,
Vitest, lint, build and browser results must come from normal exact-head CI.
A preliminary qualification is not a substitute for that final PR CI.

## Source and limits

Internal acceptance contract: unchanged masterplan sections2/3/7, GOV-03/E058.
Wire tuples are the existing source-specific P/U renderer contract; no new
normative field or code is invented. Source-family inference selects a protocol
profile only, never a legal actor, tenant, correlation target, grant or readiness
certificate. Full UNSM/field/condition/TGT/live certification remains separate.
PR319 remains stale/draft until its obsolete generic16-B assertion is replaced.

Skills: systematic debugging, TDD, differential/variant review, source-contract
verification and React server-component review. Database migrations, provider
provisioning and UI redesign are not in scope; no independent human review or
production transport execution is claimed.
